title: How big is angle IOD between two rectangles?
description: Two rectangles share the corner R, and O lies on a side of the first one. The video finds the angle between two lines at O by taking the right angle of the second rectangle and removing the part that belongs to the first.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle can be found by taking a right angle of a rectangle and subtracting the part found in a triangle. Watch for students who give the angle of the triangle at O instead of the angle that is asked for.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 5)
video_script.why: The child uses the right angles of two rectangles and the angle sum of a triangle to find an angle that is not inside any single triangle.
video_script.substitution: Use the right angle of the first rectangle in a triangle, find the angle at O, and subtract it from the right angle of the second rectangle.
video_script.anchor: rectangles PAIR and RODS sharing the corner R, with O on side AI and angle ORI marked 30 degrees
video_script.payoff_line: Angle I O D is thirty degrees

final_answer.spoken: angle I O D is thirty degrees

maths_rules: PAIR is a rectangle and O lies on AI, so angle RIO = 90 degrees
in triangle ROI: angle ROI = 180 - 90 - 30 = 60 degrees
RODS is a rectangle, so angle ROD = 90 degrees
angle IOD = angle ROD - angle ROI = 90 - 60 = 30 degrees (OI lies inside angle ROD)
check: angle ROI + angle IOD = 60 + 30 = 90 = angle ROD
video_script.design: One idea: subtract the triangle angle from the right angle of the second rectangle. The figure with both rectangles stays on the board.
